title: Email service
brief: Mail arrives from the whole internet, including a lot of spam, and must land in the right inbox. People open, search, send and attach. Never lose a message, and keep search fast even over years of mail.

clarify.q: How quickly must a new email appear in the inbox?
clarify.a: Within a few seconds. A delay of a minute is noticeable, an hour is a bug.

clarify.q: Can search be a little behind?
clarify.a: A few seconds behind is fine. It must still find mail from ten years ago.

clarify.q: Do we keep old mail on fast disks?
clarify.a: No. Recent mail is hot, older mail moves to cheaper storage. Opening it may take a bit longer.

clarify.q: Do I see my sent mail at once?
clarify.a: Yes. A sent message must show in Sent immediately, even if delivery to the other side takes longer.

notes: Most incoming mail is spam or bulk; the filter must be cheap per message (approx.).
Older mail lives in cheap storage: only the recent 150 TB is on fast disks.

Scored data retention: at least 3650 days on active authoritative stores. Copies used only for search or reports can be rebuilt. Local device history and rollup policies still require the separate protocol check.

numbers.label: Messages stored per second at peak
Search queries per second at peak

hints: A new email should be accepted fast and processed afterwards. What can hold the work in the middle?
Queue incoming mail, have workers filter and store it, and keep search in an index fed from the mailbox rather than the mailbox itself.
The index is a derived copy that can be rebuilt, not the sole durable mailbox. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: Accept mail quickly, queue it, filter and store it afterwards. The mailbox is a write-heavy store built for huge volumes, search is a separate index kept fed by a change connector, and attachments go to cheap object storage. Old mail drifts to colder tiers.

designs.name: Queue, mailbox, search index on the side
designs.why: The queue means a spam flood slows delivery a little but never refuses mail. The mailbox absorbs the writes and reads at quorum, so you always see the mail you just moved or sent. A connector copies changes into the search index, so searching never touches the mailbox and indexing never slows delivery.

tradeoffs: Filtering after queuing keeps accepting mail during a spam flood, but spam may reach inboxes a little later.
A separate search index costs extra storage but keeps heavy searches away from the mailbox.
Moving old mail to cold storage cuts cost sharply but makes opening a ten year old message slower.
Three copies in three zones cost three times the disks, and protect against a building failing.
editorial.realWorld: Large mail providers store exabytes of mail and block over 99 percent of attempted spam. Cold storage is roughly a tenth of the price of fast disks (approx.).

correctness.prompt: Email service: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Accept mail durably and keep mailbox delivery and search indexing retryable. The sender may stop retrying after acceptance, so that boundary must be durable. An external Message-ID alone is not a trustworthy globally unique dedup key. The index is a derived copy that can be rebuilt, not the sole durable mailbox.

fields.label: Step 1. Inbound mail is accepted just before a process crash. What must exist?
options: A transient queue entry scheduled after replying
Durable message bytes and a delivery intent before the success reply
fields.explanation: The sender may stop retrying after acceptance, so that boundary must be durable.

fields.label: Step 2. Mailbox delivery retries for the same accepted message. What appears?
options: One delivery record per internal delivery id and mailbox
A new inbox item for each worker attempt
fields.explanation: An external Message-ID alone is not a trustworthy globally unique dedup key.

fields.label: Step 3. Search indexing lags behind inbox delivery. Should the message disappear?
options: Read every mailbox only through the search index
No; authoritative mailbox reads work while index freshness is reported
fields.explanation: The index is a derived copy that can be rebuilt, not the sole durable mailbox.

correctness.responsibility: Accept mail durably and keep mailbox delivery and search indexing retryable.
correctness.limits: The traffic model does not execute this protocol. The checked trace covers its central responsibility; the written explanation is retained for review.

twist.brief: Demand has settled at about 2,250 requests/s. The new monthly ceiling is $12,986. The original burst reserve now competes with the operating budget. Decide which reserve to keep, then test its failure headroom. All data and recovery promises still apply.

design.name: Smaller workload, measured reserve
design.why: Reduce the paid floor for the quieter workload, preserving the required copies and recovery settings. This design was checked through the full event day.
